target_text: The main benefit is the possibility of achieving better predictive performance by learning complex feature interactions. Instead of manually deciding which FIFA statistics are important or creating many combinations of features ourselves, the attention mechanism can learn useful relationships during training. input_text: Explain the Why Do We Need This Process? section of the Attention Is All You Need research paper.
target_text: The main reason for adapting the Transformer to the FIFA dataset is to capture complex relationships between different features. A football player's performance is influenced by multiple attributes rather than a single statistic. For example, goals may be related to shots and shots on target, while passing performance may be related to successful passes, pass accuracy, and creativity. A Transformer-based approach allows these relationships to be learned through self-attention rather than considering every feature independently.

input_text: Explain the 3. Model Architecture section of the Attention Is All You Need research paper.
target_text: The Transformer follows an encoder-decoder architecture consisting entirely of attention-based components. It has 6 identical encoder layers and 6 identical decoder layers. Each encoder layer contains multi-head self-attention followed by a feed-forward neural network, with residual connections and layer normalization. The decoder contains these components plus an additional encoder-decoder attention layer. The decoder also uses masked self-attention so that it cannot look at future output words.

input_text: Explain the What Do We Gain From This? section of the Attention Is All You Need research paper.
target_text: Overall, the purpose of this project is not to reproduce the original Transformer exactly, but to adapt its central idea—self-attention—to FIFA tabular data. The original paper provides the foundation, while the FIFA dataset provides a different type of input and prediction problem. The resulting Table-Transformer uses the Transformer encoder to learn relationships between FIFA features and then uses a prediction head to produce the required output. This makes the project a practical application of the Transformer concept beyond its original natural-language-processing setting

Unlike traditional RNN- and CNN-based models, the Transformer relies mainly on self-attention and multi-head attention, allowing the model to process different elements in parallel and capture relationships between distant elements.

input_text: Explain the What Do We Gain From This? section of the Attention Is All You Need research paper.
target_text: Another advantage is parallel processing. Traditional recurrent models process sequence elements sequentially, which limits parallelization. The Transformer was specifically introduced to overcome this limitation and enable substantially greater parallelization. Although the FIFA dataset is tabular rather than sequential text, the same attention mechanism allows the feature representations to be processed together rather than forcing the model to process the features one after another.

The features are first converted into embeddings along with information about their feature identity, and then passed through the Transformer encoder. The original Transformer encoder consists of multi-head self-attention, feed-forward networks, residual connections, and layer normalization.
